title: Avoid rose charts, whose wedges grow with the square of their radius.
rule: Leave rose charts, also called polar area charts, out of every Oath & Action piece. Draw the same values as bars from one zero line, so each value is read as a length.
use_when: No reader’s question calls for it. A reader who compares amounts by month or by kind gets a truer answer from bars.

use_instead.when: The reader compares values by kind
The values run through the months of a year

text: A rose chart that sets each value as a wedge’s radius grows each wedge’s area with the square of its value: a value twice another draws a wedge four times the size. Set by area instead, the wedges still crowd together at the center, where the small ones are hard to compare. Bars draw each value as a length from one line.
why.basis: Design judgment, from the chart system our founder and editor approved in November 2026

builders: No form: the kit draws no rose chart. The sketch, work/build/guide/specimens/s-14-84-sketch.html, draws a rose chart beside bars of the same values; build the better choice with ranked-bar or column.
sketch_alt: A rose chart draws four illustrative values as wedges sized by their radius, so a value twice another looks four times as large. Bars of the same values show it twice as long.
